content.overview: Liability of the State for torts of its servants was historically limited by a sovereign/non-sovereign distinction (Kasturi Lal). Modern public-law compensation for violation of fundamental rights under Articles 32 and 226 (Rudul Sah, Nilabati Behera, D.K. Basu) substantially undercuts immunity rhetoric where constitutional rights are breached.

sections.heading: Sovereign and non-sovereign functions
sections.body: Kasturi Lal reflected a narrow approach to State liability for police-related loss in the exercise of sovereign powers. Later jurisprudence emphasises accountability and rights-based compensation.

sections.heading: Constitutional torts
sections.body: Illegal detention, custodial violence, and similar State wrongs attract public-law damages to vindicate fundamental rights. Compensation is not merely private tort damages by another name; it is a public-law remedy.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Choose the correct path: civil suit against the State/officials and/or writ petition with compensation prayer. Plead constitutional violations with facts of State action. Do not treat Kasturi Lal as the last word without checking the rights-based line of cases.

enhancement.definition: State liability in tort concerns when the Union or a State may be required to provide civil or constitutional remedies for wrongful acts of public authorities or officials.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Indian law distinguishes ordinary civil liability of the State from public-law compensation for violations of fundamental rights, with the latter developing through constitutional remedies.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Indian tort law is largely uncodified. State liability must be analysed separately under ordinary civil law and constitutional remedies, including Articles 32 and 226 where fundamental rights are implicated.
essentialIngredients: Identify State actor and legal duty
Identify wrongful act or constitutional violation
Consider statutory protection, sovereign-function arguments and constitutional limits
